feedback: D1 is a strong catalogue. You captured nine of the ten real findings with the correct class, a CWE, and a quoted evidence line each: SQL injection (A03/CWE-89 with the admin' OR '1'='1 capture at 02:15:31 and the string-concat MD5 query), MD5 hashing (A02/CWE-327, a defensible variant of CWE-916), JWT alg:none (A07/CWE-345 with Token 2), no token expiry (CWE-613), hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), stored XSS (CWE-79 with the cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443), path traversal (CWE-22 with the root:x:0:0 read at 02:24:02), open redirect (CWE-601), and the insecure cookie (CWE-614 with the setcookie line showing Secure false). The one finding you missed is XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml (A05/CWE-611, SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd), and that gap is what keeps D1 out of the high 20s. Your decoy work is exactly right: you named the b64url_decode helper, proved at the mechanism level that it only performs standard Base64URL decoding and makes no authentication decision, and correctly pointed the reader to alg:none and the hardcoded secret as the real bugs, so you earned the full decoy credit. D2 reconstructs the chain well and reconciles each hop to a capture line, from SQLi at 02:15:31 through dashboard 02:15:33, user enumeration of 312 rows at 02:16:04, stored XSS at 02:18:47, and file read at 02:24:02, with verbatim PoC blocks for the key hops. Two things hold this row down. Your CVSS vectors are complete and the SQLi vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at 9.1 matches the key exactly, but you give no justifying sentence per vector, so the vector row scores at half rather than full. Your business impact names 312 customers and the exposed fields but stops short of a naira figure, and the key wants balances summing to tens of millions tied to BoltCash with your assumptions stated, so reward yourself next time for showing the arithmetic rather than leaving it qualitative. D3 is the standout. The threat model table, the evidence-tied findings, the correctly disproved decoy, the earliest-break framing at the authentication layer, and above all the remediation order built on risk reduction per hour of effort rather than CVSS severity, with MD5 deliberately placed last because of migration cost, all hit the mark, and your two detection stopgaps both give an exact field and a false-positive rate. The only soft spot in D3 is that the executive summary ends on high security risk rather than on a customers-and-naira headline. D4 answers all four prompts in a calm, owned voice, cites ISC2 Canon I by number and load-bearing, and lands the one action you would take regardless of the manager, which is preserving and escalating the timeline through formal channels. It loses a little because the NDPA reference stays generic: you needed the section numbers, s.40 to notify the NDPC within 72 hours and s.41 to notify the 312 data subjects on high risk, tied explicitly to the customer PII. I looked for any reason to nudge this higher and the work supports the 82 honestly without inflation. The single most important fix is to catch the XXE finding in import.php and to attach a one-line justification plus a naira impact estimate to your CVSS table, since those two additions move you from strong to near-complete.
